text: Rejects pasting the content into multiple homes, and names the cost: duplicated content drifts and readers cannot tell which copy is authoritative
Picks one canonical home and names it explicitly, rather than leaving the choice open
Justifies the choice by Diataxis mode, classifying the content (largely reference, describing fixed behavior) rather than by preference
Proposes linking or cross-referencing from the other candidate locations to the canonical page, instead of copying

Recognizes that parts of the write-up may belong to different modes, for example the never-retried error list belonging with error codes, or the at-least-once rationale belonging in the explanation page
Addresses the npm README separately, since it is a different audience and surface than the docs site
States the placement rule used, so the next similar question resolves the same way
